narrative.northStar: The Warm Bakery at Golden Hour
narrative.overview: VFoods is Thailand's No.1 'ขนมปังปี๊บ' (tin-packaged biscuit/snack) maker, and the site should feel like a warm, appetizing, credible category leader. The system runs on the color of caramelizing sugar and toasted cookie — clip-orange, chocolate, and a single beam of golden highlight. The identity lives in two coordinated worlds joined by one constant orange bar: a warm, playful, mascot-led home, and sunlit warm-cream inner pages where real product photography and real SKU data do the selling. Motion is playful-but-light — CSS, native scroll, video, and pre-rendered mascot art, no WebGL/3D engine — with packet-wiggle-on-click energy in the spirit of taokaenoi/rinbee.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, food-first palette — clip-orange, chocolate, and cream; gold used only as a highlight.
Mascot-led personality: 3D-rendered snack characters carry the brand's charm.
Two worlds, one bar: warm playful home vs. sunlit cream catalog, unified by a constant orange nav.
Real over rendered on the catalog: true packshots and real dimensions, not decorative placeholders.
AA contrast is a first-class constraint — small text on light backgrounds shifts to dark red, never bright orange.
Playful-but-performant motion: CSS/native scroll/video only, no WebGL.

rules.name: The Dark-Red Small-Text Rule
rules.body: On any light background, text below ~16px must use Clip Orange #D6590C (dark red), never bright #FF6D1A, which fails WCAG AA on cream.

rules.name: The One Beam Rule
rules.body: Gold is a highlight, not a fill. It appears on at most one element per viewport — a hero accent word, a stat number, a single glow.

rules.name: The Warm-White Rule
rules.body: Backgrounds on light pages are cream (#FFF6ED) or true white for cards — never a cold gray or blue-white.

rules.name: The Light-Body Rule
rules.body: Running paragraph text is weight 300, not 400. Headlines carry the weight; body stays light.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: Every section opens with a small, wide-tracked, uppercase eyebrow in dark red or orange-soft.

rules.name: The Warm-Shadow Rule
rules.body: On light pages, every shadow is tinted orange (rgba(255,109,26,…)), never neutral black.

rules.name: The Lift-On-Intent Rule
rules.body: Cream cards are flat at rest; elevation is a response to hover/focus — ~6px of travel with a warm shadow.

dos: Do keep the nav bar orange (maroon #8E1B18 → #6E2A05 scrolled) on every page and every scroll state.
Do use dark red #D6590C for small text, tags, eyebrows, and active tabs on light backgrounds.
Do tint shadows warm on cream pages and let cards lift ~6px only on hover.
Do open every section with a wide-tracked uppercase eyebrow, and set running body copy in Sarabun weight 300.
Do use real product photography and real SKU/dimension data in the catalog.
Do lead with the mascots and keep motion playful-but-light — CSS/native scroll/video, packet-wiggle-on-click energy à la taokaenoi.
Do show the real OEM client logos (ลูกค้าของเรา/) and the cert row on the pages the brief calls for (OEM guide, home).
donts: Don't put bright #FF6D1A or gold on small text over cream.
Don't use pure #FFF as a page background or any cold gray/blue neutral — the page is warm cream #FFF6ED.
Don't carry the home's translucent glass cards onto inner pages; flatten them to solid white.
Don't reach for WebGL / a 3D engine / heavy scroll libraries — the brief never asks for it; keep it native and fast.
Don't ship a flat corporate template, a generic Bootstrap card grid, a cold minimal-white SaaS layout, or a stock-photo hero.
Don't use neutral black shadows or sharp right-angled box corners.
Don't fabricate certs, metrics, or clients — show only the five confirmed certs and the real logos in ลูกค้าของเรา/.
